implementation_notes: Foundation supplies a process-wide subject: observers register with addObserver(forName:object:queue:using:) (block form, returns an opaque token that must be removed) or the selector form, senders post with post(name:object:userInfo:), and delivery stays inside one process. It replaces the Subject/Observer pair with a name-and-object key but carries an untyped userInfo dictionary, which is why the modern API layers NotificationCenter.MainActorMessage/AsyncMessage on top for typed, actor-isolated delivery. Prefer Combine, delegates or a plain closure when the subscription is local to one object.
pitfalls: The block-based API returns a token that is only removed by an explicit removeObserver call; forgetting it keeps the closure and its captures alive, and the selector form's removeObserver(self) omission is a classic crash-on-dealloc bug.
Delivery happens on the queue you passed, or synchronously on the posting thread when queue is nil - touching UI state from a nil-queue observer is a data race.
userInfo is [AnyHashable: Any]: payload changes break receivers silently at runtime, with no compile-time signal.
NotificationCenter is global and name-based, so names collide across frameworks; application events are better served by the typed message API or a different pattern.

variants.name: Combine Publisher/Subscriber with AnyCancellable
variants.implementation_notes: Combine models the subject as a Publisher: PassthroughSubject broadcasts new values only, CurrentValueSubject also replays the latest, subscribers attach with sink/receive(on:) and hold an AnyCancellable whose deinit cancels the subscription, so unsubscription becomes lifetime management. Publishers emit only when subscribers request, which supplies backpressure, and operators (map/filter/debounce) replace the querying that observers usually do inside update. Use it when the notification is a stream to be composed; NotificationCenter alone is enough for a single fire-and-forget broadcast.
pitfalls: The subscription dies when its AnyCancellable is deallocated: storing it in a local variable (or a set that itself dies) is the classic 'publisher never fires' bug - the set must live as long as the observer.
PassthroughSubject has no replay: a subscriber that attaches after send() sees nothing, so late subscribers need CurrentValueSubject or @Published.
Values arrive on the emitting thread unless .receive(on:) is applied, so UI updates need an explicit main-queue/main-actor hop.
Combine is Apple-platform only (iOS 13/macOS 10.15 and later) and was not carried forward to non-Apple platforms, which matters for server-side or Linux Swift code.
